claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain localized nanoscale strain gradients.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons contain interfacial compositional fluctuations.
Inherent strain gradients and compositional inhomogeneities are typical of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Localized strain and compositional fluctuations disrupt or modify uniform magnetic exchange interactions.
Spatial variation in magnetic exchange interactions produces an inhomogeneous magnetic-domain structure.
The inhomogeneous magnetic-domain structure governs the magnetocaloric response under low-field cooling cycles.
The inhomogeneous magnetic-domain structure governs magnetic hysteresis under low-field cooling cycles.
Controlled post-deposition annealing can relieve, homogenize, or reconfigure nanoscale strain gradients.
Controlled post-deposition annealing can mitigate compositional variability.
Annealing-induced homogenization of strain and composition reduces variance in local magnetic interactions.
Reducing variance in local magnetic interactions produces a more spatially uniform and reversible magnetocaloric response.
Controlled annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Controlled annealing will modify, potentially enhance, or make the magnetocaloric response more reversible relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Strain homogenization after annealing improves heat-transfer efficiency.
As-deposited films or nanoribbons exhibit significant hysteresis.
As-deposited nanoscale structural heterogeneity alters the magnetocaloric effect.
Low-field operation is exemplified by applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
Cooling-cycle frequency is limited by nanoscale heat-transfer rates.
Higher fields or different thermal cycles may produce bulk-like behavior for which the proposed mechanism does not hold.
The proposed mechanism may cease to dominate when sample dimensions eliminate dominant interfacial effects.
